post.description:
Creates a discount voucher for a given storefront.

**Prerequisites:**

- Vouchers apply only to **new** products. Used products are not eligible: a voucher is never offered on a used-product PDP and does not discount used-condition units, even if their product ID or EAN is included in the voucher.

`title` is the display name of the voucher.

`storefront` is the storefront code (e.g. `de`, `cz`, `sk`) for which the voucher is valid.

`discount_type` defines how the discount is applied. Must be one of: `PERCENTAGE`, `ABSOLUTE`.

`discount_amount` is the value of the discount. For `PERCENTAGE` discounts the maximum allowed value is `85`.

`begin_at` and `end_at` define the validity period of the voucher. Both must be valid dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. `begin_at` must be today or later, `end_at` must be today or later, and `end_at` must be on or after `begin_at` (the same date can be used for both to create a voucher active for today only).

`usage_limit` is the maximum number of times the voucher can be redeemed. Must be at least `1`.

Either `products` (a list of product IDs) or `eans` (a list of EAN strings) must be provided to scope the voucher to specific items.

A single voucher can cover at most **3000 items**. This applies to `products` and `eans` individually and to the two lists combined; exceeding it returns `400`. To cover a larger assortment, split it across several vouchers.

**Vouchers are scoped per product, not per unit.** Most SellerAPI endpoints operate on units (a seller's specific listing of an item), but a voucher created here applies to **every new-condition unit owned by the calling seller** whose item matches one of the provided product IDs or EANs. There is no way to scope a voucher to a single unit.

`export_to_third_parties` is an optional flag that controls whether the voucher is shared with third-party price-comparison portals. Defaults to `false`.

Returns a paginated list of vouchers. All parameters are optional.

`storefront` filters by one or more storefront codes. Pass the parameter multiple times to filter by several storefronts (e.g. `?storefront=de&storefront=cz`). When omitted, vouchers across all storefronts are returned.

`status` filters by voucher lifecycle state. Pass the parameter multiple times to filter by several statuses (e.g. `?status=active&status=new`). Allowed values: `new`, `active`, `inactive`, `expired`, `consumed`, `deleted`. When omitted, vouchers of all statuses are returned.

`search_term` filters by campaign name or voucher ID.

`id_product` filters vouchers that apply to one or more specific products. Pass the parameter multiple times to filter by several products (e.g. `?id_product=123&id_product=456`). When omitted, vouchers for all products are returned.

`ean` filters vouchers that apply to one or more products identified by EAN. Pass the parameter multiple times to filter by several EANs (e.g. `?ean=4006381333931&ean=4006381333948`). When omitted, vouchers for all products are returned.

`sort` orders results in the form `field:direction`, where `field` is one of `products`, `redemptions`, `beginAt`, `createdAt`, `totalSales`, `roas`, `acos` (`products` sorts by the number of products attached to the voucher), and `direction` is `asc` or `desc` (e.g. `?sort=redemptions:desc`).

`limit` must be between 1 and 100 (default: 30). `offset` must be a multiple of `limit`.

get.description:
Kaufland groups your product with closely comparable products from other sellers. These are
separate products, not offers on the same product page, so there is no real Buy Box between
them. But shoppers who come across them in search treat them as interchangeable and usually
take the cheapest one, so in practice they compete like a Buy Box does. This endpoint ranks
up to 10 products in that group the same way, so you get the whole picture in one call
instead of checking product by product.

Each array entry describes the ranking for one product in the group: `id_product`, `storefront`,
`condition`, `num_units` (total number of offers for that product and condition), and `units`
(the ranked list of offers). Each unit has `buybox_rank` (1 is the winning offer), `seller`,
`price` and `shipping_rate` (both in the minor currency unit), `delivery_time_min`/`_max` in
days, `fulfillment_type` (`fulfilled_by_merchant` or `fulfilled_by_kaufland`), `condition`, and,
only when you own the unit, `id_unit` and `id_offer`.
